definition_en: an area of sand or small stones beside the sea
core_image: 退潮后留下细密波纹的金色沙滩
scene: 潮水退去，沙面还留着波纹。Children built a castle on the beach.
sceneCN: 这里 beach 是「海滩」（第 1 个义项：海边由沙或小石子铺成的平地）；句意是孩子们在海滩上堆城堡。

derivatives.zh: 由 beach 加 -y 构成，义为「有海滩气息的」

senses.title: The sandy edge of the sea
senses.definition: an area of sand or small stones beside the sea

senses.why: This sense grew from an old word for a stream, then shifted to the shore it reached.

senses.title: To pull a boat ashore
senses.definition: to pull or drive a boat onto the shore
senses.definitionCN: 把船拖上或冲上岸
senses.example: The storm beached the small boat.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴把小船冲上了滩。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, so to beach a boat is to put it on the beach.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，把船放上海滩就是使船搁浅。

intro.en: Beach began as a word for a stream and moved to the shore.

definition_en: a line of light, a strong horizontal bar, or a happy smile
core_image: 阳光从窗缝里斜射成一道光柱
scene: 门缝里漏进一道亮线。A beam of light fell across the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 beam 是「光束」（第 1 个义项：成束射出的光线）；句意是一束光落在地板上。

derivatives.zh: 由 beam 加 -ing 构成，义为「喜气洋洋的」
由 sun 与 beam 复合，义为「阳光光束」

senses.title: A line of light
senses.definition: a narrow line of light
senses.definitionCN: 成束射出的细长光线
senses.example: A beam of light fell across the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一束光落在地板上。
senses.why: Light was once pictured as a straight wooden beam, so the word moved to rays.
senses.whyCN: 人们曾把光线想象成笔直的木梁，于是这个词转指光线。

senses.title: A strong horizontal bar
senses.definition: a long strong bar that supports a building
senses.definitionCN: 支撑建筑的坚固长条材料
senses.example: Workers raised a steel beam into place.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把钢梁吊装到位。
senses.why: This was the older sense, from a word for a tree or plank.
senses.whyCN: 这是更早的义项，源头是表示树木或木板的词。

senses.title: To shine or smile widely

senses.example: She beamed at the good news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到好消息她笑了。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, first for shining light and then for a shining face.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，先指发光，再指脸上放光般的笑容。

intro.en: Beam first meant a tree or plank, then a ray of light and a smile.

definition_en: the seed of a climbing plant used as food, or a seed like it

definition_en: a large heavy wild animal, or to carry, endure or give birth
core_image: 一头棕熊在河岸边直立张望
scene: 河水很急，他还是咬牙撑住了。She could not bear the cold any longer.

senses.title: A large wild animal
senses.definition: a large heavy wild animal with thick fur

definition_en: to hit repeatedly, to defeat someone, or a regular rhythm

scene: 鼓声一下一下压过人群的喧闹。The drums beat a steady rhythm.

definition_en: an alcoholic drink made from grain
core_image: 杯壁挂着水珠的一扎冰啤酒
scene: 夏夜的院子里摆着几张矮桌。They shared a cold beer after work.
sceneCN: 这里 beer 是「啤酒」（第 1 个义项：用谷物酿成的含酒精饮料）；句意是下班后他们一起喝了杯冰啤酒。

derivatives.zh: 由 beer 加 -y 构成，义为「啤酒味的」
由 beer 与 house 复合，义为「啤酒馆」

senses.title: A drink brewed from grain
senses.definition: an alcoholic drink made from grain
senses.definitionCN: 用谷物酿成的含酒精饮料
senses.example: They shared a cold beer after work.
senses.exampleCN: 下班后他们一起喝了杯冰啤酒。
senses.why: The word came from an old term for a strong drink.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自一个表示烈性饮料的旧词。

senses.title: A glass or serving of beer
senses.definition: a glass or bottle of beer
senses.definitionCN: 一杯或一瓶啤酒
senses.example: We ordered two beers.
senses.exampleCN: 我们点了两杯啤酒。
senses.why: The uncountable drink became countable when it meant a serving.
senses.whyCN: 不可数的饮料在表示「一份」时变成可数。

intro.en: Beer goes back to a Latin word for a drink.
intro.cn: beer 可追溯到拉丁语中表示饮料的词。

items.en: biber meant a drink.
beor meant a strong drink.
ber named ale brewed from grain.
items.cn: ber 指谷物酿造的麦酒。

items.en: beer settled as the name of this drink.
items.cn: beer 定型为这种饮料的名称。

items.en: beer is drunk cold in many countries.
items.cn: 如今许多国家习惯冰镇饮用。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one sound; the near-meaning group gives other drinks.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音；近义组是其他饮品词。

normalIntro.en: Beer is a grain drink, counted in glasses or bottles.
normalIntro.cn: beer 是谷物饮料，论杯或论瓶计数。

normal.en: Beer as a drink is uncountable.
normal.cn: 作饮料时 beer 不可数。

normal.en: Two beers means two servings.
Draft beer comes from a barrel.
normal.cn: draft beer 指从桶里打出的生啤。

normal.en: A beer glass is shaped for beer.
normal.cn: beer glass 是喝啤酒用的杯子。

normal.en: Go for a beer means go out to drink.
normal.cn: go for a beer 指出去喝一杯。

abstract.en: See beads of water on a cold glass.
abstract.cn: 想象冰杯壁上挂着水珠。

abstract.en: See white foam rising in a glass.
abstract.cn: 想象杯中升起的白色泡沫。

abstract.en: See friends at a small table on a summer night.
abstract.cn: 想象夏夜里围坐小桌的朋友。

examples.en: They shared a cold beer after work.
examples.cn: 下班后他们一起喝了杯冰啤酒。

examples.en: We ordered two beers.
examples.cn: 我们点了两杯啤酒。

examples.en: He poured the beer slowly into a glass.
examples.cn: 他把啤酒慢慢倒进杯里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 beer 想成杯壁上挂满水珠的那一扎冰啤。

root: 可追溯到拉丁语 biber「饮料」，经古英语 beor「烈性饮料」与中古英语 ber 演变而来，现代专指用谷物酿造的啤酒。

sensesIntro.en: The drink itself, and one serving of it.
sensesIntro.cn: 既指啤酒这种饮料，也指一份啤酒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cold glass of beer covered in droplets.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯壁挂满水珠的冰啤酒。

intro.en: Beer takes -s and -y, and joins house in a compound.
intro.cn: beer 可加 -s、-y，也能与 house 复合。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is biber, a drink.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 biber，意为「饮料」。

definition_en: earlier than something, or in front of
core_image: 天还没亮，厨房的灯先亮了
scene: 闹钟还没响，他就已经醒了。He left before the sun rose.
sceneCN: 这里 before 是「在……之前」（第 1 个义项：时间上早于某事）；句意是太阳升起之前他就离开了。

derivatives.zh: 由 before 与 hand 复合，义为「事先」
与 before 同源，义为「前部的」

senses.title: Earlier in time
senses.definition: earlier than a time or event
senses.definitionCN: 时间上早于某个时刻或事件
senses.example: He left before the sun rose.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳升起之前他就离开了。
senses.why: The word was built from be- and an old word for in front.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 be- 与一个表示「在前面」的旧词构成。

senses.title: In front of
senses.definition: in front of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在某人的前面或某物的前面
senses.example: She stood before the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她站在门前。
senses.why: Time and place shared one word, since what is ahead comes first.
senses.whyCN: 时间与空间共用一个词，因为「在前」也就意味着「在先」。

senses.title: At an earlier time
senses.definition: at an earlier time, used alone
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用，表示过去某个更早的时候
senses.example: I have met him before.
senses.exampleCN: 我以前见过他。
senses.why: The adverb use grew from the same idea of being earlier.
senses.whyCN: 副词用法同样来自「更早」这一概念。

intro.en: Before is an old compound meaning in front.
intro.cn: before 是一个古老的复合词，意为「在前面」。

items.en: foran meant in front.
beforan meant in front of.
beforan shrank to before.
before covered both time and place.
before works as preposition, conjunction and adverb.
items.cn: 如今 before 可作介词、连词与副词。

note.en: The look-alike group begins with be-; the near-meaning group gives words for earlier or ahead.
note.cn: 形近组都以 be- 开头；近义组表示更早或在前。

normalIntro.en: Before marks what comes earlier, in time or in place.
normalIntro.cn: before 标记更早发生的事，或更靠前的位置。

normal.en: Before dawn means earlier than sunrise.
The day before means the previous day.
normal.cn: the day before 指前一天。

normal.en: Before long means soon.
Beforehand means in advance.
The word is unchanged in form.

abstract.en: See a kitchen light on before sunrise.
abstract.cn: 想象日出前亮起的厨房灯。

abstract.en: See a person waiting in front of a door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人等在门前。

abstract.en: See a remembered face from long ago.
abstract.cn: 想象很久以前见过的一张脸。

examples.en: He left before the sun rose.
examples.cn: 太阳升起之前他就离开了。

examples.en: She stood before the door.
examples.cn: 她站在门前。

examples.en: I have met him before.
examples.cn: 我以前见过他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 before 想成「站在时间的前面」，先到的那一步。

root: 由古英语 be- 与 foran「在前面」构成 beforan「在……前面」，中古英语缩合为 before，同时用于时间与空间，并发展出副词「以前」。

sensesIntro.en: Earlier in time, in front in space, and earlier on its own.
sensesIntro.cn: 时间上更早、空间上在前，以及单独使用的「以前」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kitchen light already on before sunrise.
core.cn: 核心意象：日出前就先亮起的厨房灯。

intro.en: Before is a fixed word, and it builds beforehand.
intro.cn: before 是固定词，可与 hand 构成 beforehand。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自古英语。

items.meaning: earlier than or in front of

definition_en: a person who lives by asking for money or food
core_image: 寒风里缩在墙角的一个破旧身影
scene: 街角的石阶上坐着一个人。A beggar held out an empty bowl.
sceneCN: 这里 beggar 是「乞丐」（第 1 个义项：靠乞讨为生的人）；句意是一个乞丐伸出一只空碗。

pos.zh: 动词：使贫穷；使难以描述

derivatives.zh: 由 beggar 加 -ly 构成，义为「贫穷的」
由 beggar 加 -y 构成，义为「乞讨；极度贫穷」
beggar 的基础动词，义为「乞讨」

senses.title: A person who begs
senses.definition: a person who lives by asking others for money or food
senses.definitionCN: 靠向他人讨钱或讨食为生的人
senses.example: A beggar held out an empty bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 一个乞丐伸出一只空碗。
senses.why: The word came from an old French name for a member of a begging order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古法语中称呼乞讨教团成员的名称。

senses.title: To make poor or beyond words
senses.definition: to make someone poor, or to be too strange to describe
senses.definitionCN: 使某人贫穷，或奇特得无法描述
senses.example: The war beggared the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 战争使整个地区陷入贫困。
senses.why: The noun became a verb meaning to reduce to beggary.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，表示使人沦为乞丐般的贫穷。

intro.en: Beggar first named a member of a religious begging order.
intro.cn: beggar 最初指某个以乞讨为生的宗教教团成员。

items.en: begard named a member of a begging order.
items.cn: begard 指乞讨教团的成员。

items.en: begger meant a person who begs.
beggar became the usual spelling.
the noun also became a verb.
beggar belief means too strange to believe.
items.cn: 如今 beggar belief 指难以置信。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives other poor or homeless words.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是其他表示贫穷或流浪的词。

normalIntro.en: A beggar asks for money, and to beggar is to make poor.
normalIntro.cn: beggar 是讨钱的人，作动词则指使人贫穷。

normal.en: The plural is beggars.
Beg is the short verb behind it.
normal.cn: beg 是它背后的短动词。

normal.en: Beggar belief means too strange to believe.
Beggar description means too odd to describe.
Beggary means great poverty.

abstract.en: See a figure crouched in a cold corner.
abstract.cn: 想象寒风里缩在墙角的身影。

abstract.en: See an empty bowl held out.
abstract.cn: 想象伸出的空碗。

abstract.en: See a ruined town after war.
abstract.cn: 想象战后破败的城镇。

examples.en: A beggar held out an empty bowl.
examples.cn: 一个乞丐伸出一只空碗。

examples.en: The war beggared the whole region.
examples.cn: 战争使整个地区陷入贫困。

examples.en: Such rudeness beggars belief.
examples.cn: 这样的无礼令人难以置信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 beggar 想成墙角那只伸出来的空碗。

root: 源自古法语 begard，原指以乞讨为生的宗教教团成员，中古英语写作 begger，后定型为 beggar；名词又转为动词，表示使贫穷。

sensesIntro.en: The person who begs, and the act of reducing to poverty.
sensesIntro.cn: 既指乞讨的人，也指使人陷入贫穷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure crouched in a cold corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：寒风里缩在墙角的身影。

intro.en: Beggar takes -s, -ing, -ly and -y endings.
intro.cn: beggar 可加 -s、-ing、-ly、-y 后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word came through French.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词经法语传入。

definition_en: to start doing something or to start happening
core_image: 跑道上运动员弯腰等待发令枪
scene: 发令枪还没响，跑道上一片安静。The race will begin at noon.
sceneCN: 这里 begin 是「开始」（第 1 个义项：开始做某事或开始发生）；句意是比赛将在中午开始。

derivatives.zh: 由 begin 加 -ning 构成，义为「开始」
由 begin 加 -ner 构成，义为「初学者」

senses.title: To start doing or happening
senses.definition: to start an action or an event
senses.definitionCN: 开始某个动作或事件
senses.example: The race will begin at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛将在中午开始。
senses.why: The word was built from be- and an old verb meaning to open or start.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 be- 与一个意为「开启、开始」的旧动词构成。

senses.title: To start from something
senses.definition: to have something as the first part
senses.definitionCN: 以某事物作为第一部分
senses.example: The course begins with the basics.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从基础开始。
senses.why: The phrase begin with arose from the idea of a first point.
senses.whyCN: begin with 这一搭配来自「起始点」的概念。

intro.en: Begin is an Old English compound of be- and a verb for starting.
intro.cn: begin 是古英语中由 be- 与表示开始的动词构成的复合词。

items.en: ginnan meant to begin.
beginnan meant to begin or undertake.
biginne kept the same sense.
begin settled into its modern forms.
begin is one of the commonest verbs of starting.
items.cn: 如今 begin 是最常用的「开始」动词之一。

note.en: The look-alike group shares be- or a similar sound; the near-meaning group gives other start verbs.
note.cn: 形近组共享 be- 或相近读音；近义组是其他表示开始的动词。

normalIntro.en: Begin means to start, and begin with names the first part.
normalIntro.cn: begin 指开始，begin with 指以某物作为开头。

normal.en: The past tense is began.
The past participle is begun.
The present participle is beginning, with double n.
normal.cn: 现在分词是 beginning，双写 n。

normal.en: To begin with means firstly.
A beginner is a person who is starting.

abstract.en: See a runner bent at the starting line.
abstract.cn: 想象跑道上弯腰的运动员。

abstract.en: See a gun about to sound.
abstract.cn: 想象即将响起的发令枪。

abstract.en: See a first page turning.
abstract.cn: 想象翻开的第 一页。

examples.en: The race will begin at noon.
examples.cn: 比赛将在中午开始。

examples.en: The course begins with the basics.
examples.cn: 这门课从基础开始。

examples.en: She began to laugh.
examples.cn: 她笑了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 begin 想成起跑线前弯腰待发的那一刻。

root: 由古英语 be- 与 ginnan「开始」构成 beginnan「开始、着手」，经中古英语 biginne 演变为今天的 begin，核心义为「开始」。

sensesIntro.en: To start an action, and to start from a first point.
sensesIntro.cn: 既指开始一个动作，也指从某个起点开始。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner waiting at the starting line.
core.cn: 核心意象：起跑线前等待的运动员。

intro.en: Begin takes -ning and -ner endings and doubles the final n.
intro.cn: begin 加 -ning、-ner 时双写末尾的 n。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自古英语。
